title: The Abdomen
question: Which organ is glowing?
lines: Can you name this glowing organ?
These are the organs of the belly, from the front.
Which organ is it?
It sits high on the body's right side, under the ribs.
It's the largest organ inside your body.
It's A. The liver.
Why it matters: it clears toxins from blood and makes bile for fat.

title: The Abdomen
question: Which organ is glowing?
lines: Most people can't place this organ. Can you?
We're looking from behind now.
Which organ is glowing?
It lies behind the stomach, across the upper belly.
It makes insulin and digestive enzymes.
It's D. The pancreas.
Why it matters: type 1 diabetes destroys its insulin-making cells.

title: The Abdomen
question: Which organ is glowing?
lines: This J-shaped organ is where your food goes after the esophagus.
Look at the J-shaped organ on the patient's left side.
Which organ is glowing?
The spleen sits behind it and filters blood. It doesn't digest food.
Its acid and muscle churn food into a thick liquid.
It's A. The stomach.
Why it matters: its acid helps break down food and kills many germs.

title: The Abdomen
question: Which part of the colon is it?
lines: The colon has four parts. Can you name this one?
Look at the S-shaped section low in the belly.
Which part of the colon is glowing?
The descending colon runs down the patient's left side first.
This part curves like an S before it reaches the rectum.
It's D. The sigmoid colon.
Why it matters: it holds waste briefly before the rectum.

title: The Abdomen
question: Which part of the gut is it?
lines: A wide tube wraps around the inside of your belly.
Watch the glowing tube that frames the abdomen.
Which part of the gut is it?
The small intestine is narrower and coiled in the middle.
This wide tube is the colon, made of four parts.
It's B. The large intestine.
Why it matters: it absorbs water from what's left of your food.
